accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the NETA app is correct?
o: It enables voters to rate their elected representatives and was built by a private start-up.
It is used exclusively for filing election petitions before the High Courts.
It was conceptualised and developed by the Election Commission of India.
It enables citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations with geo-tagged photographs.
accepted.x: The NETA app allows voters to rate their representatives and was built by a private start-up, not conceptualised by the Election Commission of India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the private NETA app from official Election Commission applications.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cVIGIL:
1. It enables citizens to report violations of the Model Code of Conduct.
2. Photographs or videos accompanying a complaint may be geo-tagged.
3. The system provides for action within 100 minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos, with action envisaged within 100 minutes.
accepted.tq: Check whether all three operational features belong to the same application.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s: ECINET is associated with which one of the following functions?
o: Merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites into one platform
Issuing election petitions directly to the Supreme Court
Providing only postal ballots to service voters
accepted.x: ECINET is a unified platform that merges more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institutional function of the named digital platform.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s:
The Voter Helpline app is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
1. Searching for a name in the electoral roll
2. Filing forms and complaints
3. Reporting violations through geo-tagged videos only
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Voter Helpline app helps users search the electoral roll and file forms and complaints. Reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos is associated with cVIGIL.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related functions of different Election Commission apps.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s:
Which of the following categories of electors are entitled to use postal ballots?
1. Service voters
2. Special voters
3. Electors on election duty
4. Persons in preventive detention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The listed categories—service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and persons in preventive detention—are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a statutory-category list rather than recalling a single category.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?
o: Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd; silver nitrate
accepted.x: Indelible election ink is manufactured by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd and is based on silver nitrate.
accepted.tq: Use the manufacturer–ingredient pair to avoid a two-part factual trap.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Voter Helpline app — Search name in electoral roll
ECINET — Exclusive platform for election petitions
accepted.x: ECINET is a unified platform merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites; it is not an exclusive platform for election petitions.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched purpose among closely related electoral initiatives.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s:
Consider the following measures relating to polling stations:
1. The maximum number of electors assigned to a polling station is 1,200.
2. A facility is provided for depositing mobile phones at polling booths.
3. Candidate booths are to be located just beyond 100 metres from the polling station.
4. Candidate photographs on EVMs have been redesigned in colour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The measures include a 1,200-elector cap, mobile-deposit facilities, colour candidate photographs on EVMs and candidate booths just beyond 100 metres from polling stations.
accepted.tq: Treat each administrative measure as an independent statement and verify the complete set.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in State Legislative Assemblies
Article 332 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 334 — Establishment of the Election Commission
accepted.x: Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies.
accepted.tq: Use the Article–institution pairing and reject neighbouring-Article swaps.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
With reference to reserved Lok Sabha constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Amalapuram is a Scheduled Caste-reserved constituency.
2. Araku is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
3. Tirupati is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Amalapuram and Tirupati are Scheduled Caste-reserved constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, whereas Araku is the Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between SC and ST constituencies within the same State.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the reservation pattern in the Lok Sabha for Telangana?
accepted.x: Telangana has three Scheduled Caste-reserved and two Scheduled Tribe-reserved Lok Sabha constituencies.
accepted.tq: Compare the State-wise SC/ST figures without reversing the categories.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (State)
A. Andhra Pradesh — Lok Sabha
B. Andhra Pradesh — Legislative Assembly
C. Telangana — Lok Sabha
D. Telangana — Legislative Assembly

List-II (Number of SC/ST reserved seats)
1. 4 / 1
2. 29 / 7
3. 3 / 2
4. 19 / 12

Code:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC and 1 ST Lok Sabha seats and 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats. Telangana has 3 SC and 2 ST Lok Sabha seats and 19 SC and 12 ST Assembly seats.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure State–House pair and then complete the numerical matching.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the allocation of SC and ST reserved constituencies?
1. ST seats are generally located where the share of the ST population is highest.
2. SC seats are spread across the State and rotated at each delimitation.
3. All voters in a reserved constituency, and not merely voters belonging to the reserved community, may vote.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: ST seats are concentrated in areas with the highest ST population share, SC seats are spread and rotated at delimitation, and reserved constituencies have a common electorate of all voters.
accepted.tq: Combine location, rotation and electorate principles in one reservation question.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 334 is correct?
o: The original period of reservation was 5 years and it ended in 1955.
The Article deals exclusively with reservation in local bodies.
The provision originally applied for 20 years, up to 1970, without later extension.
The original period of reservation was 10 years, up to 1960, and it has been repeatedly extended.
accepted.x: Article 334 originally provided for a ten-year period, up to 1960, and the reservation period has been repeatedly extended by constitutional amendments.
accepted.tq: Use the original time limit and the subsequent-extension feature together.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Anglo-Indian representation is correct?
1. The President could nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
2. The Governor could nominate one Anglo-Indian to a State Legislative Assembly.
3. These provisions were ended by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Articles 331 and 333 provided for nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha by the President and one to a State Assembly by the Governor. The 104th Amendment ended these provisions.
accepted.tq: Check the authority, number and constitutional termination together.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
The constitutional provision for reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies under the 106th Amendment provides for which of the following?
1. One-third reservation of seats
2. Reservation for 15 years
3. Rotation after each delimitation
4. Immediate operation irrespective of census and delimitation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 106th Amendment provides one-third reservation for 15 years, with rotation after each delimitation. Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation; therefore statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the false immediacy claim in a statement about commencement of constitutional reservation.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s: A constituency having no fixed geographical boundary, such as the Sangha seat in Sikkim, is known as a:
accepted.x: A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary. The Sangha constituency in Sikkim is an example in which only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact electoral term from its defining geographical feature.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
With reference to the Sangha constituency in Sikkim, consider the following statements:
1. It is an example of a floating constituency.
2. Only registered Buddhist monks can vote and contest in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The Sangha seat has no fixed geographical boundary and is restricted to registered Buddhist monks as electors and candidates.
accepted.tq: Test both defining features of a special constituency rather than just its name.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s:
Match the type of election with its description:

List-I
A. General election
B. Mid-term election
C. By-election

List-II
1. Election to a legislature dissolved before expiry of its normal term
2. Election held for a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months
3. Election held at the normal end of the legislature’s term

Code:
accepted.x: A general election is held at the normal end of a legislature’s term, a mid-term election follows premature dissolution, and a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.
accepted.tq: Match each election type with its timing and purpose.
accepted.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

accepted.s: Under Section 80 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, an election can be called in question only by means of:
o: A writ petition before the District Court
A reference by the Election Commission
accepted.x: Section 80 provides that no election can be called in question except by an election petition. The constitutional basis is Article 329(b).
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory bar in Section 80 from the filing period in Section 81.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s: An election petition under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, must ordinarily be presented within:
o: 45 days of the election of the returned candidate
60 days of the declaration of poll
30 days of the notification of election
90 days of the constitution of the House
accepted.x: Section 81 requires an election petition to be presented within 45 days of the election of the returned candidate.
accepted.tq: Separate the 45-day filing period from the separate Section 80 rule and Section 100 grounds.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s: Which court ordinarily tries an election petition under the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Supreme Court in the first instance
accepted.x: Under Section 80A, an election petition is tried by the High Court. An appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the court of original trial and distinguish it from the appellate court.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s:
Consider the following grounds for declaring an election void under Section 100 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. The returned candidate was not qualified or was disqualified.
2. A corrupt practice was committed.
3. A nomination was improperly rejected.
4. Improper acceptance of votes or breach of the Constitution or the Act affected the result.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four circumstances are recognised grounds under Section 100 for declaring an election void, subject to the statutory requirements concerning their effect on the election result where applicable.
accepted.tq: Test the complete statutory list of grounds rather than relying on a single familiar ground.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding disposal of election petitions is correct?
o: The Supreme Court tries every election petition directly and no appeal is permitted.
The Election Commission must decide the petition within six months, with no appeal.
The District Court must decide the petition within three months, with appeal to the High Court.
The High Court is required to try to decide the petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
accepted.x: The High Court should try to decide an election petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Use the court hierarchy and time expectation to reject authority swaps.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present legal location of electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation?
o: They remain in IPC Chapter IXA only.
They are contained in BNS Chapter IX, Sections 169 to 177, from 1 July 2024.
They are dealt with only under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are contained in the Constitution under Article 329(b).
accepted.x: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation are placed in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Sections 169–177. Earlier, they were in Chapter IXA of the IPC.
accepted.tq: Track the transition from the IPC provision to the corresponding BNS chapter and sections.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s:
Match the following provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 with their contents:

List-I
A. Section 80
B. Section 80A
C. Section 81
D. Section 100

List-II
1. Grounds for declaring an election void
2. Petition to be presented within 45 days
3. No election may be called in question except by an election petition
4. Election petition to be tried by the High Court

Code:
accepted.x: Section 80 contains the election-petition bar, Section 80A specifies the High Court, Section 81 prescribes 45 days, and Section 100 lists grounds for declaring an election void.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive Section 80 and Section 100 pairs, then resolve the two procedural provisions.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The rule that an election cannot be called in question except by an election petition is contained in Section 80 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Reason (R): Section 81 prescribes the period within which an election petition must be presented.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, but the 45-day filing period under Section 81 does not explain the separate rule in Section 80 requiring an election petition to question an election.
accepted.tq: Separate two true neighbouring statutory provisions and test whether the Reason actually explains the Assertion.
accepted.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds
